findings.claim: Balkan-Turk culture already reaches mainstream audiences through TV and comedy creators: TRT1's 'Balkan Ninnisi' and Kosovo-origin comedian Selviye İnci (~1M Instagram followers in 2022).
findings.detail: An article from 8 Aug 2022 describes Selviye İnci (born Istanbul 1983; family came from Kosovo in 1955) as known for Instagram and YouTube sketches in Balkan dialect, with about 1M followers (@selviye_inci). She was cast in TRT1's 'Balkan Ninnisi', a series about the Evlad-ı Fatihan Balkan Turks; its official account has ~29K followers (snapshot). On TikTok, I saw a video by @rumeliabalkan ('Balkanica') listed at ~211.7K views and a Balkan-Turk migration-story video by @_tturkic with ~18.4K likes. I could not verify account-level TikTok counts.
findings.recommendation: Use dialect, humor and recognition hooks ('Rumelili ninelerin dediği...') as entry points into the history content. Later, a guest Reel with a Balkan-dialect creator could bring a big early jump in followers. Watch what TikTok accounts like @rumeliabalkan and @_tturkic post to see which formats work.
findings.verify_note: TikTok returned only a page shell. Instagram returned 429, so the ~29K for @balkanninnisitrt and Selviye İnci's current follower count are unverified. Her 1M figure is from 2022.
findings.corrected_claim: The canlitv.com article of 8 Aug 2022 says Selviye İnci (@selviye_inci) was born in Istanbul in 1983. Her family is originally from Kosovo and migrated in 1955. She had nearly 1M Instagram followers and was cast as 'Güldaniye Hala' in TRT1's Balkan Ninnisi. The TikTok handle in the cited URL is @rumelibalkan, not @rumeliabalkan as the finding writes it. Its per-video counts (~211.7K views) and the @_tturkic figures could not be verified.

findings.claim: Existing content in this niche clusters around 1923 mübadele, the 1989 exodus from Bulgaria, regional identity, and music or dialect. The 1352–1912 period of Ottoman Rumeli (conquest, cities, figures, the 1912 loss) has no strong Turkish-language social media home.
findings.detail: This is my synthesis of N2–N6, N10 and N18. The large Instagram accounts are identity pages. Search results for 'mübadele' are dominated by 1923 stories. Widely marked anniversaries (from the sources) are 30 Jan for mübadele and the 1989 exodus (3 Jun–21 Aug 1989; more than 350,000 people left; events in Turkey marked the 35th anniversary in 2024). Rumeli history channels on YouTube are under 2K subscribers, and I found no Rumeli-history Instagram page with significant reach.
findings.recommendation: Keep the 1352–1912 identity but connect it to the community's existing emotional dates. For example, 30 Jan: 'Selanik'te 560 yıl nasıl başladı?'; the June 1989 anniversary: 'Kırcaali'nin Osmanlı kuruluşu'; October, 1912 anniversary: a Balkan War series. Run a recurring 'Şehir şehir Rumeli' series (Üsküp, Manastır, Selanik, Filibe, Prizren, Saraybosna, Yanya) so each sub-community has a reason to share.
sources: no source; synthesis of findings above
findings.verify_note: The researcher's '3 Jun–21 Aug 1989; more than 350,000' did not appear in the sources I opened. The BTA piece is paywalled after the lead. The point that the 1352–1912 history slot is empty is a synthesis, and Time Balkan's existing 'Balkanlar Tarihinde Bugün' section partly weakens it.
findings.corrected_claim: The 35th anniversary of the 1989 exodus from Bulgaria was marked by events in Turkey (BTA, 31 May 2024). Per Time Balkan (4 Nov 2019), forced departures began after Zhivkov's 29 May 1989 statements and peaked in June–August 1989. 345,960 people reached Turkey within a year, and the total reached about 360,000 with a later wave in the second half of 1990. The mübadele anniversary statement on 30 Jan is confirmed for 2026.

findings.claim: There are a few English-language Ottoman and Balkan history accounts and channels. They are useful as references or collab partners, but none I found focuses on Rumeli in Turkish.
findings.detail: @ottomanarchive (Ottoman Imperial Archives): ~38K followers, 4,157 posts, active through June 2026 (snapshot); a picture account on Ottoman history with a Patreon link. On YouTube, small English channels such as Balkan Mode (videos with 42–625 views in Oct 2026) cover Ottoman Rumelia. Large English history channels get millions of views (The Great War, Balkan Wars, 2.81M).
findings.recommendation: Optionally add short English subtitles on Reels to reach English-speaking Balkan and diaspora viewers. Contact @ottomanarchive about cross-sharing archival photos, with credit and permission.
findings.verify_note: Instagram was blocked (429), so I could not check @ottomanarchive's ~38K followers, 4,157 posts or June 2026 activity. The Balkan Mode view counts and The Great War's 2.81M come from YouTube search pages, which I did not re-query because the search budget was gone.

missed_points: Verification limit: WebSearch was not available for this check because the shared budget of 200 searches per turn was already used. The user can ask for a follow-up once the search budget is available again.

Time Balkan already runs a recurring 'BALKANLAR Tarihinde Bugün' history section, for example a Yahya Kemal Üsküp-to-Istanbul piece (https://timebalkan.com/). The '1352–1912 history slot is empty' claim should be softened. Time Balkan is a partner and also a partial content competitor.

The Edirne Balkan History Museum (Hıdırlık Tabyası) presents itself as covering '600 years of Turkish history in the Balkans' (Hurriyet Daily News, 1 Jan 2022, https://hurriyetdailynews.com/key-bastion-to-serve-as-battlefield-museum-170468). That framing is almost the same as '560 Yıl Rumeli', which makes the museum a natural partner for on-site Reels and reposts.

Another umbrella body: Karadeniz Rumeli Dernekleri Federasyonu signed the 30 Jan 2026 mübadele statement (https://www.kentvebellek.com/haber/balkan-derneklerinden-mubadele-103-yili-bildirisi_194/). Several signatories are Cretan (Girit) mübadil groups, so 30 January content aimed at the whole coalition should also cover Crete, not only Rumeli.

The federation president's 2018 population claim was 'about 30 million' (Kamuran Atakan, https://www.sondakika.com/guncel/haber-85-rumeli-balkan-dernegi-iftar-programinda-bulustu-10901868/). The researcher's 'more than 30M' overstates it.

DataReportal's own note says its 2026 Turkey platform figures are ad-reach estimates, not monthly active users (https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2026-turkey). The TÜİK survey (https://www.haberler.com/teknoloji/internet-kullanan-bireylerin-orani-yuzde-92-3-oldu-20118584-haberi/) is the better measure of actual use: WhatsApp 90.0%, YouTube 77.6%, Instagram 71.1%, ages 16–74, 2026.

Academic network: Trakya University was elected president of the Balkan Universities Association, which was founded in Edirne on 21 April 2014, according to RUÇAM's Rumelian Media Report Issue 3, April 2026 (https://rucam.rumeli.edu.tr/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/RMRIngilizce3.pdf). That is another route to university accounts and Balkan academics.

Several 'live' items are actually old. The Belene camp exhibition at the Bursa Göç Müzesi was in December 2019 (https://www.yeniakit.com.tr/haber/belene-kampini-canlandirdilar-968217.html), and Selviye İnci's ~1M follower figure is from August 2022 (https://canlitv.com/blog/balkan-ninnisine-surpriz-oyuncu). Both need a fresh check before outreach.

summary: Research run 2026-11-03/04. Instagram's own statements say that for people who don't follow you yet, DM sends count slightly more than likes (Mosseri, Jan 2025). The calendar should therefore favour posts people forward to relatives: old city names, family migration stories, Rumeli dialect, then-vs-now photos. Educational or 'tarihte bugün' posts that people only like are less useful. Five 2025-2026 platform changes matter for this page. (1) Since April 2026, accounts that mostly repost others' photos or carousels lose recommendations. Every archive image needs its own research, text or voiceover on top. (2) Trial Reels need 1,000 followers, so they are not available on launch day. (3) Hashtags are capped at 5 and mainly help search, so captions must carry keywords. (4) Insights now show Skip Rate, the share of viewers who leave in the first 3 seconds, which is the hook test. (5) Collab posts let up to 5 accounts co-author a post, which is the fastest legitimate way to borrow other audiences. The verified anniversary calendar is unusually strong right at launch. Selanik's surrender protocol was signed 8 Nov 1912 and the city handed over on 9 Nov. Varna (1444), Atatürk's death and Kırklareli's 1922 liberation all fall on 10 Nov. Thracian towns' 1922 liberation days run 13–25 Nov, followed by Manastır, Çatalca and Albania later in November 1912. After that come 26 Dec 1984 (Bulgaria name-change protests), 29–30 Jan (Western Thrace resistance day, Lausanne exchange convention), 26 Mar 1913 (Edirne falls), 6 May (Hıdrellez), May–June 1989 (the Bulgarian Turks' exodus) and 15/28 June (Kosovo 1389). The page's founding date 1352 (Çimpe) and Edirne's conquest date (1361 vs 1369) are disputed by historians. Use that openly as myth-busting content rather than hiding it. Image sources: the Library of Congress Abdul Hamid II albums include 1880s–90s photos of the Manastır military school and the Yanya and Edirne high schools. SALT Research images are CC BY-NC-ND, which bans cropping, colourising and text overlays. Türkü recordings carry neighbouring rights even when the song itself is anonymous. Use a Creator account (not Business) and Instagram's in-app music library, or your own voiceover. No sourced case study of a fast-growing Turkish Rumeli history page was found, and 'Shadows of Rumelia' did not appear in the search index. The closest verified examples are crowdsourced Balkan family-photo archives and local then-vs-now accounts. Those grew steadily rather than explosively.

findings.claim: Instagram's head said the top three ranking signals are watch time, likes and sends. Sends count slightly more for 'unconnected' reach, meaning people who don't follow you yet, which is exactly the growth audience.
findings.detail: Social Media Today, 22 Jan 2025, quoting Mosseri: 'The top three signals that matter most for ranking are watch time, likes and sends' and 'Likes are slightly more important for connected content, and sends are slightly more important for unconnected content.' He told creators to watch average watch time, likes per reach and sends per reach. Third-party claims that sends weigh '3-5x more than likes' have no Meta source and should be ignored.
findings.recommendation: Judge every post by sends per reach first. Write content that gives people a reason to forward it to a specific person ('Selanikli dedene gönder', 'Kırcaalili arkadaşını etiketle/gönder'). Stop reading likes as the success measure for growth posts.
findings.verify_note: I opened the SMT article dated 22 Jan 2025. It quotes Mosseri: 'The top three signals that matter most for ranking are watch time, likes and sends' and 'Likes are slightly more important for connected content, and sends are slightly more important for unconnected content.' No Meta source for '3-5x' was found. Method note: the WebSearch budget for this turn was already used up, so every check in this review was done by fetching cited or primary pages directly with WebFetch.

findings.claim: Since 30 April 2026, accounts that mainly repost other people's photos or carousels are ineligible for recommendations (Explore, suggested posts). Reels were already covered. Many history pages work exactly this way.
findings.detail: TechCrunch, Tubefilter and PetaPixel all reported it on 30 Apr 2026. Followers still see the posts, but they stop reaching new people. 'Original' includes third-party material that is meaningfully transformed with 'unique text, creative edits, and voiceover' or added commentary and context. Changing speed or adding a screenshot of the source's name is not enough. Planoly and SociallyIn describe a rolling 30-day majority test with recovery once most recent posts are original. Tubefilter does not confirm that threshold, so treat it as unverified. When copies are identical, Instagram surfaces the original instead and notifies its creator. Meta says 75% of recommended content in the US is now classified as original.
findings.recommendation: Never post a bare archive photo or a clip taken from another page. Every post needs your own research layer: a Turkish voiceover, a map, a then-vs-now pairing, a caption with sources, or a design template unique to the page. Do not repost Shadows of Rumelia-style content. Keep a 30-day log showing most posts are self-produced.
findings.verify_note: The primary source, Instagram's own blog post and original-content guidelines, confirms the date, scope and 75% figure. Three corrections. (a) Instagram uses a rolling 30-day window for regaining eligibility at a 'significant percentage', not a stated majority. 'Primarily' is undefined. (b) 'Notifies the original creator' appears only in Planoly. The official post does not say it. (c) Most important for this page: the recommendation lists 'a caption with sources' and a 'design template' as originality layers, but Instagram explicitly says captions, credits and borders are not material edits. A bare archive photo with a sourced caption most likely still counts as unoriginal. The guidelines do not mention archival or public-domain photos at all. Instagram also says you can check standing under Account Status and appeal. TechCrunch and Tubefilter, both 30 Apr 2026, match.
findings.corrected_claim: Instagram's 30 Apr 2026 update: accounts that primarily post unoriginal photos or carousels, as well as Reels, are no longer shown where Instagram recommends content. Posts still reach existing followers. Original content means content you made yourself, or third-party content materially edited with text that adds context (not text that only describes what is shown), graphics that add information, remix, or voiceover. Instagram says these do NOT count: borders, watermarks, speed changes, screenshots, credits, or 'a different caption or superficial additions.' Eligibility returns when a 'significant percentage' (no number given) of recent posts over a rolling 30-day window is original. 75% of US recommendations now come from original posts.

findings.claim: Trial Reels (a test that shows a Reel only to non-followers first) were opened in July 2025 to public accounts with at least 1,000 followers, so the page cannot use them at launch.
findings.detail: Instagram launched Trial Reels on 10 Dec 2024. Mosseri announced the expansion on Threads in July 2025 (BetaNews, 14 Jul 2025; Social Media Today). Trials stay off your grid and out of followers' feeds. A reported daily cap of about 20 trials is not officially confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Make 1,000 followers the first milestone. After it, use Trial Reels to A/B-test hooks for the same story: for example, an old-name hook against a date hook against a family hook.
findings.verify_note: SMT, 13 Jul 2025: Mosseri confirmed the expansion to public accounts with 1,000+ followers. Instagram's Creators blog dates the Trial Reels launch to 10 Dec 2024 and confirms trials are shown to non-followers first and kept off the grid. It names no follower threshold and points to the Help Center. BetaNews returned 403. I could not check whether the threshold is still current in Nov 2026.

findings.claim: Instagram has capped hashtags at 5 per post or Reel since December 2025. Mosseri says hashtags help search but do not by themselves increase reach, so captions and on-screen text must carry the keywords.
findings.detail: Mosseri announced on 19 Dec 2025: 'We're now limiting hashtags to a maximum of five per post.' The previous maximum was 30. Reported by Business Today and Social Media Today.
findings.recommendation: Use at most 5 tightly relevant tags, for example #Rumeli #Balkan #muhacir #mübadele #Selanik. Put searchable words in the first caption line and on screen: city names in both Turkish and the current local form, 'Batı Trakya', 'Bulgaristan Türkleri', '1989 göçü'.
findings.verify_note: The 5-tag limit and the previous 30 are confirmed. The attribution and quote are wrong. Both SMT (dated 18 Dec 2025) and Business Today (19 Dec 2025) credit the @creators account, not Mosseri. The quoted line 'We're now limiting hashtags to a maximum of five per post' does not appear in either. The real wording describes a gradual rollout.
findings.corrected_claim: Instagram's official @creators account said on Threads around 18-19 Dec 2025 that it 'will gradually update' the hashtag limit for posts and Reels to five, down from 30. Mosseri has separately said hashtags 'don't work' to increase reach.

findings.claim: Instagram added Skip Rate (the share of viewers who leave within the first 3 seconds) and a retention chart to Reels insights in August 2025. That gives the page a measurable hook test.
findings.detail: Skip Rate replaced the older View Rate (Social Samosa, Aug 2025; Metricool). Reels with low reach may show no value because Meta does not publish the minimum view count. No official Meta statement was found that skip rate is a direct ranking factor, so claims that it is should be ignored.
findings.recommendation: Review Skip Rate after every Reel. If it is high, rework the first second: move the answer or image forward and drop logo and title intros. Keep a log of which opening types work (see H1).
findings.verify_note: Social Samosa, 25 Aug 2025: Skip rate is the share of viewers who skip before 3 seconds. It replaces View rate, and the retention chart is a new addition. That article also said rollout was expected 'in the coming weeks.' Metricool, 4 Feb 2026, still says Instagram 'will soon replace' view rate, so availability may vary by account or region. Neither source mentions a minimum view threshold. Ask the user to check that the metric appears in their own insights.

findings.claim: Collab posts let up to 5 collaborators co-author one post. It appears on every co-author's grid and reaches all their audiences, which is the main legitimate way to borrow established Rumeli audiences.
findings.detail: The limit was 3 co-authors when Meta's newsroom announced it in August 2023 and is now 5 (Sked, Vista Social and others). Each co-author must accept. Vendor claims of '3.8x reach' are unverified. Guides disagree on whether co-authors can be added after publishing.
findings.recommendation: Plan one collab per week from week 2. Candidates: Balkan or Rumeli migrant associations, Western Thrace Turkish associations, Thracian municipalities and kent müzeleri (city museums) on their liberation days (13–25 Nov), and local-history pages. Offer them a finished, sourced carousel about their town so the collab costs them nothing.
findings.verify_note: Sked (published 22 Aug 2026, modified 9 Oct 2026) cites Instagram's Help Center 'as of October 2026': up to five collaborators, six accounts including the creator. Vista Social agrees. Both say collaborators can be added after publishing, which settles the researcher's open point. The Help Center page itself did not render via fetch. Instagram's 30 Apr 2026 originality post also names Collabs as a recommended way to credit others.
findings.corrected_claim: A collab post can carry up to 5 invited collaborators plus the original author, so up to 6 accounts in total. Collaborators can be invited after publishing via Edit > Tag people, and each must accept.

findings.claim: No sourced case study was found of a Turkish Rumeli or Balkan history Instagram page growing fast in 2024–2026, and 'Shadows of Rumelia' did not appear in search results at all.
findings.detail: Searches run: 'Shadows of Rumelia Instagram'; Turkish queries on tarih sayfası growth, Rumeli/Balkan Instagram accounts and muhacir photo campaigns; English queries on history creator case studies for 2025. The only peer-reviewed Turkish study found covers three history-meme pages (@tarihselmizah, @mizahsentarih, @avartarih) in the Turkish History Education Journal, 26 Oct 2025. It reports no follower or engagement numbers. Its findings: content is dominated by military and political events and leaders, while social and cultural history and women are 'minimally represented'.
findings.recommendation: Don't copy growth numbers from blogs. The gap the study identifies is the page's opening: everyday Rumeli life (food, dialect, weddings, migration, women's stories) rather than only battles. Use the competitor's ~8000 followers as a benchmark only once you can verify the number yourself in the app.
sources: no source found for Shadows of Rumelia (search run 2026-11-03)
findings.verify_note: DergiPark confirms the study: 'Tarih konulu memler: İnstagram üzerinden bir inceleme' by Günakan, Ulaş, Güney and Erol Şahin, Turkish History Education Journal 14(2): 82-103, 26 Oct 2025. It covers @tarihselmizah, @mizahsentarih and @avartarih and says only 'substantial follower base', with no numbers. Military and political content dominates, and social and cultural history, scientists, artists and women are minimally represented. I could not verify 'Shadows of Rumelia'. WebSearch was unavailable, and direct fetches of the guessed handles instagram.com/shadowsofrumelia, /shadows.of.rumelia and /shadows_of_rumelia all redirected to login (HTTP 302).

findings.claim: Verified Balkan precedents show that crowdsourced family archives work in this region. Followers or donors send old family photos, and the account curates them.
findings.detail: @thebalkanarchive was started by Bulgaria-born, UK-based researcher Milena Vassova to tell a Balkan history 'from within' (New East Digital Archive, Feb 2021). Balkanism (Arbër Qerka-Gashi) began posting family photos in April 2020. Balkan Image Archive was crowdsourced from late 2020. Bulgarian Visual Archive, launched in 2019, holds 16,000+ images, many donated, and invites the public to supply captions (RFE/RL, 6 Oct 2024). None of these sources gives follower numbers.
findings.recommendation: Launch a submission series in week 1 (see H3, 'Dedemin Bavulu'). Ask for one photo, the town of origin, the year of migration and a two-line story. Collect written permission in DMs before posting, and credit the family. These posts produce comments, sends among relatives, and original content that counts under P2.
findings.verify_note: Partly checked. Bulgarian Visual Archive is confirmed by RFE/RL (6 Oct 2024): launched 2019, 16,000+ 20th-century images, many from personal collections, captions open to anyone with verifiable knowledge. The New East Digital Archive article returned HTTP 503, so I could not recheck the @thebalkanarchive founder (Milena Vassova), Balkanism (April 2020) or Balkan Image Archive details. No source gives follower or growth figures, so 'work' means these projects exist, not that they grew fast.

findings.claim: Then-vs-now city accounts build durable, place-loyal audiences, but the documented ones grew steadily over years, not virally.
findings.detail: Old Vintage Melbourne has about 50k followers (Time Out, undated). Nostalgia Maine started in April 2020 and passed 12,000 followers by November 2024 (Press Herald, 25 Nov 2024). Old New Vienna has 11,500+ followers (vienna.at, undated). Their pull is identification with a place.
findings.recommendation: Use then-vs-now as a weekly anchor, not the growth engine. Pair it with old city names and family prompts so each post invites sends and comments. Examples: an Abdul Hamid II-era photo of a Manastır or Yanya school beside the same spot today; an old Selanik postcard beside the modern street.
findings.verify_note: The Time Out article is dated 23 Jan 2023, not undated. The Press Herald gives about 12,400 in its info box and 'more then 12,000' in the text. vienna.at failed DNS resolution. The conclusion, steady rather than viral growth, rests on only two checked examples.
findings.corrected_claim: Old Vintage Melbourne (@oldvintagemelbourne) had about 50k followers per Time Out, 23 Jan 2023. Nostalgia Maine, started April 2020, had about 12,400 followers per the Press Herald, 25 Nov 2024. I could not recheck Old New Vienna.

findings.claim: Ranked by expected sends plus comments for a muhacir-descended Turkish audience (my own reasoning, not measured).
findings.detail: 1) Old Turkish names of Balkan cities with a 'Aileniz hangi şehirden?' prompt. Identity drives both comments and sends. 2) Migration-story submissions (dedenin/ninenin fotoğrafı). Highest emotional pull, produces comments and saves. 3) Rumeli dialect quizzes ('Bu kelimeyi bilen Rumelili'). Strong sends between relatives. 4) Then-vs-now. Strong sends. 5) Surname and origin prompts. High comments, but high risk of factual error. 6) 'Tarihte bugün' Reels tied to November 1912 and 1922 dates. Timely, moderate. 7) Animated maps (1352→1912 territorial change). High watch time and shares, but heavy to produce. 8) Food and recipes (pırasalı börek etc.). Saves. 9) Myth-busting (Çimpe 1352, Edirne 1361/1369, the Kosovo assassination legend). Comments, with some risk of arguments in the comments. 10) Folk songs. Emotional, but copyright-limited (F5).
findings.recommendation: Weekly mix for the first 8 weeks: 2 identity or UGC posts (1–2), 1 dialect quiz, 1 then-vs-now carousel, 2–3 'tarihte bugün' or Balkan War Reels, and 1 map or myth-buster. Re-rank after 30 days using your own sends per reach and comments per reach.
sources: no source; reasoning based on P1 (sends drive unconnected reach) and P8 (Balkan family-archive precedents)
findings.verify_note: The researcher labels this as their own reasoning, and no source exists. It is consistent with P1 (sends weigh more for unconnected reach). Given the corrected P2, though, any format built on bare archive images (then-vs-now, old postcards) needs real on-image context, a voiceover or new graphics, not just a caption. Otherwise the account risks losing recommendations.

findings.claim: Rumeli dialect quizzes can be sourced from academic glossaries, so the page does not have to invent words.
findings.detail: An Edirne regional glossary of about 7,000 words is drawn from TDK's Türkiye'de Halk Ağzından Derleme Sözlüğü (Paradigma Akademi, 2023). A 2022 İnönü University PhD thesis on the Turkish dialect of Şumnu (Shumen) is based on recordings from 47 villages and includes a word list. Németh's 1956 West/East Rumeli classification gives quiz angles. For example, Western dialects end words in -i where standard Turkish has ı/u/ü ('alti', 'buldi').
findings.recommendation: Run a weekly 'Rumeli Sözlüğü' series. Each card: the word, its meaning, the region, the source (TDK Derleme Sözlüğü or thesis), and a CTA such as 'Ninen bunu nasıl söylerdi? Yorumlara yaz'. Comments will add new words and local variants, which feed future posts.
findings.verify_note: I extracted the PDF text myself. 'About 7,000 words' is confirmed, but the glossary is not drawn from TDK alone. The source tags on each entry suit the quiz idea well. The İnönü thesis page returned 403, so I could not recheck it. I did not open the Németh/Günşen or Dialectologia sources.
findings.corrected_claim: 'Edirne Yöresi Söz Varlığı' (Doç. Dr. Muharrem Özden, Edirne 2023, about 290 pages) contains about 7,000 words. It was compiled from the 6-volume TDK 'Türkiye'de Halk Ağzından Derleme Sözlüğü' plus 7 other regional works such as local dialect theses, and each entry is tagged with its source (e.g. 'DS.1866: Sarıcaali-Edirne').

findings.claim: Old-name content is the most shareable format, but tone decides whether it reaches the whole diaspora or invites brigading and mass reports from Greek, Bulgarian or Macedonian accounts.
findings.detail: Authoritative sources for Turkish exonyms: Turkey's 2007 UNGEGN submission, which lists exonyms for Europe compiled from old Turkish maps and documents, and Wikipedia's lists of Turkish exonyms (one for Greece specifically, for Gümülcine, İskeçe, Dedeağaç, Yanya, Selanik and others). Tone and moderation risk is my own reasoning.
findings.recommendation: Frame these posts as memory and belonging ('Selanik — bugün Thessaloniki; 1912'ye kadar...') rather than territorial claims. Show both names. Moderate comments in the first hour and pin a sourced comment. Possible series name: 'Kayıp Adlar' / 'Eski Adıyla'.
findings.verify_note: The UN document E/CONF.98/32, 'Turkish exonyms (2002-2007)', was submitted by Turkey (BEGeoN_T), dated 27 June 2007, for the 9th UNCSGN. It describes a 'List of exonyms of Europe and neighbouring regions of Turkey' compiled 'by examining both contemporary and old Turkish maps and documents.' I did not check the Wikipedia mirror. The tone and brigading part is the researcher's reasoning.

findings.claim: Surname content can hook on the Soyadı Kanunu (Surname Law) anniversary, but no source was found that muhacir families systematically took town-based surnames ('Selanikli', 'Üsküplü').
findings.detail: Law no. 2525 was adopted 21 June 1934 and published in the Resmî Gazete on 2 July 1934. Under the implementing regulation, families chose surnames from 2 Jan 1935 to 2 July 1936. Searched for town-name surname patterns among migrants: not found.
findings.recommendation: On 21 June 2027, run a prompt ('Soyadınız Rumeli'den bir yer adı mı?') and collect followers' stories. Do not publish claims like 'X surname means Balkan origin' without a source.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed from the academic article text: Law 2525 was adopted 21 June 1934 and published in Resmî Gazete no. 2741 on 2 July 1934. The Soy Adı Nizamnamesi (RG 2891, 27 Dec 1934) sets the window '2/1/1935 günlemecinden 2/7/1936 günlemecine kadar', and after that date governors assign surnames. English Wikipedia's 'two years' wording is looser and should not be used. I did not search for town-based muhacir surnames.

findings.claim: Türkü in Reels: an anonymous folk melody may be free, but almost every recording carries neighbouring rights for 70 years. Business accounts are also limited to Meta's royalty-free Sound Collection.
findings.detail: Turkish copyright law (FSEK m.82, per secondary legal sources) protects performers, phonogram producers and broadcasters for 70 years from the relevant event. Only third-party guides cover the Business-account restriction. They agree on it but disagree on whether switching to a Creator account restores the full library everywhere. Tracks picked inside the app are covered by Instagram's licences. The same audio ripped and uploaded may be muted, and library tracks can be muted later if licences change. Whether anonymous türkü melodies count as protected works under FSEK is disputed (Hürriyet column); no definitive source found.
findings.recommendation: Use a Creator account, not Business. Use türkü only from Instagram's in-app library, a recording you commission or perform yourself, or none. Make a Turkish voiceover your default audio: it is original audio and counts toward originality (P2). Never upload TRT archive or YouTube recordings.
findings.verify_note: The law-firm tool says FSEK m.82 neighbouring rights run 'ilgili olaydan itibaren 70 yıl', and author rights run life plus 70 (m.27). Foximusic (updated 2 Oct 2026) says Business accounts are limited to the Meta Sound Collection of about 14,000 tracks, while creator accounts get 'broad (nearly full)' access. Both are secondary sources. Foximusic adds that the Sound Collection licence does not carry over when a Reel is reposted to other platforms, which matters for E5 cross-posting.

findings.claim: Hook patterns for history Reels: put the payoff or the striking image in the first 1–2 seconds and test with Skip Rate. Third-party guides agree on 1–3 seconds. Meta's own figure could not be confirmed.
findings.detail: Planoly (educational Reels) says the first 1–2 seconds must be interesting, give the payoff up front, and take yourself out of the narrative. Other guides say about 3 seconds. Example hooks for this page (my own wording): (a) 'Bu şehrin 1912'ye kadarki adı neydi?' over a drone or archive shot; (b) 'Dedeniz bu limandan geldiyse...'; (c) a date-and-number shock: '8 Kasım 1912: Selanik ve 26.000 asker teslim edildi'. The 26,000 figure comes from popular sources, so check it before use; (d) a before/after slider; (e) a map zooming from Edirne to Üsküp. Avoid logo or title intros.
findings.recommendation: Script each Reel as hook (0–2s) → 3 facts with sources (to ~40s) → a send or comment CTA. Cut opening logos. Edit in Instagram's free Edits app (launched April 2025), which exports without watermark.
findings.verify_note: The Planoly content matches, but its date is wrong. The BetaNews page on the Edits launch returned 403, so I did not recheck the April 2025 date or watermark-free export. Edits clearly exists: Instagram's blog shows Edits posts in Sept-Oct 2026, including a carousel editor dated 7 Oct 2026.
findings.corrected_claim: Hook advice of 'first 1 to 2 seconds have to be interesting' and 'Put the climax first, and explain later!' comes from a Planoly educational-Reels article last updated 8 Mar 2021, not 2025. The 26,000 Selanik figure appears in English Wikipedia's Hasan Tahsin Pasha article, which is still a tertiary source.

findings.claim: Captions and CTAs should name the action and the person. Comment-to-DM automation is allowed through Meta-partner tools when the user starts the exchange.
findings.detail: Vendor and policy summaries (Planoly, ManyChat, Creatorflow) agree. Keyword-triggered DMs through official Meta APIs are allowed. Cold outreach is not. Messages must fall within the 24-hour window and deliver exactly what was promised. Mass DM broadcast via the API has been restricted since Feb 2024. Growth statistics from DM vendors are unverified. Carousels can now hold 20 slides (Aug 2024), which suits 'save' content such as maps and timelines.
findings.recommendation: Rotate three CTA types. Send: 'Bunu Gümülcineli birine gönder.' Comment: 'Aileniz hangi köyden? Yaz, haritaya ekleyelim.' Save: 'Kaydet: 1352–1912 Rumeli fetih kronolojisi (20 slayt).' Optionally, 'HARİTA yaz, PDF'i DM'den gönderelim' through a Meta-partner tool. Do not automate cold follows or DMs.
findings.verify_note: The researcher compressed the timing into 'must fall within the 24-hour window.' The first reply to a comment actually has 7 days (Planoly, updated 23 Oct 2026; Creatorflow, updated 30 Oct 2026). The Feb 2024 broadcast pause is supported only second-hand through Creatorflow. The 20-slide carousel (Aug 2024) was not rechecked because PetaPixel returned 403.
findings.corrected_claim: Comment-to-DM via Meta's Private Replies API is allowed. A comment permits ONE private reply within 7 days. Further messages are allowed only after the user replies, inside a 24-hour window that resets with each reply. The limit is 750 private-reply calls per hour. Automated DMs to people who have not engaged are banned. Meta paused Instagram DM broadcast lists in Feb 2024, per the ManyChat Help Center as cited by Creatorflow.

findings.claim: Use a small set of named recurring series so followers know what is coming and come back (my own reasoning).
findings.detail: Suggested series: 'Bugün 1912' (Balkan War day by day, Nov 2026–May 2027, see D1/D6/D7); 'Kayıp Adlar' (old city names); 'Dedemin Bavulu' (follower migration stories); 'Rumeli Sözlüğü' (dialect); 'Şehir Kartı' (then-vs-now); 'Mit mi, Gerçek mi?' (disputed dates such as 1352 and 1361/1369); 'Kurtuluş Takvimi' (Thrace 1922 liberation days, with municipality collabs). Each series gets a fixed visual frame that matches the archival-seal logo.
findings.recommendation: Pick 4 series for launch: Bugün 1912, Kayıp Adlar, Dedemin Bavulu, Rumeli Sözlüğü. Run each on a fixed weekday, give each a Highlight cover, and add the rest after 1,000 followers.
sources: no source; reasoning based on P1, P6, P8 and the verified calendar D1–D9
findings.verify_note: This is the researcher's own reasoning with no source. Nothing to refute.

findings.claim: November 2026 opens with verified Balkan War centenary-plus dates: Selanik 8/9 Nov, Manastır 16–19 Nov, Çatalca 17–18 Nov, Albania 28 Nov, armistice 3 Dec 1912.
findings.detail: Selanik: the surrender protocol was signed 8 Nov 1912 (26 Oct Old Style; the Ottoman Rumi calendar gives the same date) and the handover was carried out the next day, 9 Nov (Wikipedia, Hasan Tahsin Pasha). Some Turkish academic works give 9 Nov, which is a debated date. Battle of Monastir/Manastır: 16–19 Nov 1912. First Battle of Çatalca: 17–18 Nov 1912 (4–5 Nov Old Style); one article says 16–17. Albanian independence declared at Vlorë: 28 Nov 1912. Armistice: 3 Dec 1912 (20 Nov Old Style).
findings.recommendation: Launch 4 Nov with a manifesto Reel ('Neden 560 yıl?'). Run a 'Bugün 1912' countdown 5–7 Nov, a major Selanik Reel and carousel on 8 Nov, and 'Selanik'te son gün' on 9 Nov. On 16–19 Nov, connect Manastır with the Abdul Hamid II photos of the Manastır military school (E1). Use 17–18 Nov for 'Çatalca: İstanbul'un kapısında durdurulan ordu'.
findings.verify_note: Wikipedia confirms the Selanik protocol on 8 Nov 1912 NS (26 Oct OS), the handover 'carried out the next day' (9 Nov), and the 26,000 men. Monastir was fought 16-19 Nov 1912 and the city entered 19 Nov. First Çatalca was 17-18 Nov 1912 NS (4-5 Nov OS). Albania declared independence at Vlorë on 28 Nov 1912. I did not recheck the armistice of 3 Dec 1912 in this pass, though it matches standard references.

findings.claim: 10 November carries three anniversaries: Atatürk's death (1938; he was born in Selanik in 1881), the Battle of Varna (10 Nov 1444), and Kırklareli's 1922 liberation. Kırklareli itself holds its celebrations on 11 Nov.
findings.detail: Varna, 10 Nov 1444: Ottoman victory; King Władysław killed (Britannica, Wikipedia). Kırklareli came under Turkish administration on 10 Nov 1922 (TÜBA local history), but ministry news shows the 101st-anniversary ceremonies held on 11 Nov 2023. Atatürk: born 1881 in Selanik; 19 May is a symbolic birthday he chose himself, and the actual day is unknown.
findings.recommendation: On 10 Nov, post one respectful piece ('Selanik'ten Ebediyete') with no quizzes, jokes or growth tricks. Move Varna (1444) to 9 or 11 Nov, or mention it briefly. Do Kırklareli on 11 Nov to match local practice, and offer the municipality or kent müzesi a collab.
findings.verify_note: The disagreement is about the liberation date itself, not only about when local ceremonies are held. Wikipedia notes that Władysław's death is uncertain. The recommendation to post on 11 Nov still holds. I did not recheck Atatürk's birth details, which are standard.
findings.corrected_claim: Varna was fought 10 Nov 1444 and was an Ottoman victory. Władysław III was generally assumed killed, but his body was never found, so his exact fate is debated. Kırklareli's 1922 liberation date itself varies by source: TÜBA says 10 Nov 1922, while a 10 Nov 2021 TBMM speech says '11 Kasımda Kırklareli ilimiz'.

findings.claim: The Eastern Thrace liberation days of November 1922 give almost daily, collab-ready local anniversaries from 13 to 25 Nov. Several dates differ between sources.
findings.detail: Tekirdağ: 13 Nov 1922 (TÜBA). Malkara and Hayrabolu: 14 Nov (TBMM speech). Şarköy: 17 Nov. Uzunköprü: 18 Nov; the Greek authorities had renamed it 'Makrifere' (Wikipedia). Keşan: 19 Nov (2024 local news marking the 102nd anniversary). İpsala: 20 Nov (TBMM, 2021; single source). Havsa: 23 Nov. Edirne: 25 Nov 1922 (ministry page; one news item says 24 Nov), with Edirne's liberation week running 17–27 Nov. Dates before the launch window: Çorlu 1 Nov; Vize 1 or 2 Nov. Debated: Lüleburgaz 8 or 9 Nov, Pınarhisar 8 Nov, Babaeski 9 Nov. Some sources list Greek evacuation dates in October, which explains the conflicts.
findings.recommendation: Make a 'Kurtuluş Takvimi' carousel template (town, date, one archival image, one fact) and post on each local date, tagging or co-authoring with the municipality. Check each date against the municipality's own site first. Build the Edirne 25 Nov piece as the series climax.
findings.verify_note: Most dates are confirmed, but the citations need fixing. The cited TÜBA ch05 PDF is the Kırklareli chapter (I extracted it, and it gives Kırklareli 10 Nov). It does not support Tekirdağ 13 Nov, which comes from the 2021 TBMM speech. That speech gives Vize as 1 Nov, not '1 or 2'. Wikipedia confirms Uzunköprü's Greek-era name 'Makrifere' and 18 Nov. Still check each date with the municipality before posting.
findings.corrected_claim: Per Tekirdağ MP Enez Kaplan's TBMM speech of 10 Nov 2021, these places were liberated in November 1922: Çorlu, Ergene and Vize on 1 Nov; Muratlı 2 Nov; Lüleburgaz and Pınarhisar 8 Nov; Babaeski and Pehlivanköy 9 Nov; Kırklareli, Kofçaz and Demirköy 11 Nov; Tekirdağ 13 Nov; Malkara and Hayrabolu 14 Nov; Şarköy 17 Nov; Uzunköprü 18 Nov; Keşan and Meriç 19 Nov; İpsala 20 Nov; Havsa and Enez 23 Nov. Edirne was liberated 25 Nov 1922 (Edirne provincial directorate), with celebrations running 17-27 Nov (TBMM, 2012).

findings.claim: December: Plevne surrenders 10 Dec 1877; North Macedonia's Turkish Education Day is 21 Dec; Bulgaria's 'Revival Process' protests were 26 Dec 1984.
findings.detail: Siege of Pleven/Plevne: 20 Jul–10 Dec 1877; Osman Pasha surrendered after a failed breakout and was later titled 'Gazi' (Britannica). 21 Aralık Türkçe Eğitim Bayramı marks Turkish-language schooling granted in 1944 and became an official holiday in North Macedonia in 2007. Revival Process: a forced name-change campaign launched December 1984 that renamed 800,000+ people (RFE/RL, 30 Jan 2025). Protests in Momchilgrad (Mestanlı) on 26 Dec 1984. In Mogilyane the same day, militia fire killed a 17-month-old girl named Türkan (BNR). Her surname 'Feyzullova' was not confirmed in sources found. The campaign's end date (early 1985) is not precisely sourced.
findings.recommendation: 10 Dec: a Plevne Reel. 21 Dec: a collab or greeting with North Macedonian Turkish organisations. Around 24–27 Dec: a solemn 'İsmim Benimdir' carousel with sources. Invite followers from Bulgaria to share how their own names were changed, with consent and an option to stay anonymous.
findings.verify_note: The BNR link cited for Mogilyane now returns 404. RFE/RL (30 Jan 2025) names Momchilgrad and Gruevo but not Mogilyane, and gives no date of death. RFE/RL says restrictions lasted until 1989. Kure Ansiklopedi confirms 1944 and Feb 2007 for 21 Dec. Britannica (Plevne) returned 403, so I did not recheck 10 Dec 1877, though it is the standard date.
findings.corrected_claim: The Revival Process began in December 1984 and forcibly renamed 800,000+ people in about three months. Protests in Momchilgrad on 26 Dec 1984 were met with water cannon, batons and live rounds. RFE/RL reports that a 17-month-old girl, Turkyan, was brought to hospital dead on arrival and 'died amid police violence in 1984'. The village (Mogilyane) and the exact date are not confirmed in the sources available. 21 Dec Turkish Education Day dates from 1944 and was made official by a February 2007 amendment to North Macedonia's holidays law.

findings.claim: Late January could run as a 'Mübadele and Minority Week': 23 Jan 1913 Bab-ı Ali coup (over Edirne), 29 Jan 1988 Western Thrace National Resistance Day, 30 Jan 1923 Lausanne population exchange convention.
findings.detail: The Raid on the Sublime Porte on 23 Jan 1913 brought back the Unionists, who refused to give up Edirne. War resumed 3 Feb 1913 (Second Çatalca). On 29 Jan 1988, more than 10,000 Western Thrace Turks marched in Gümülcine after the Turkish Youth Union and İskeçe Turkish Union were closed; the day is commemorated annually. The Lausanne exchange convention was signed 30 Jan 1923, with the compulsory exchange starting 1 May 1923 under Article 1. Estimates give about 1.2 million Orthodox and 355,000–400,000 Muslims.
findings.recommendation: Run a 5-day arc, 26–31 Jan 2027. Pair a mübadil family submission call with a sourced explainer carousel. Approach Western Thrace associations for a 29 Jan collab.
findings.verify_note: Wikipedia confirms the Raid on the Sublime Porte on 23 Jan 1913, triggered by fears of ceding Edirne. Haber7 (2022) quotes Doç. Dr. Ali Hüseyinoğlu: on 29 Jan 1988, more than 10,000 Western Thrace Turks gathered in Gümülcine, the first time that many had come together. That article does not name the closed associations, so that detail is unverified here. The Lausanne convention was signed 30 Jan 1923, with the compulsory exchange from 1 May 1923 (Art. 1). Wikipedia gives about 1.2 million Greeks and about 400,000 Muslims.

findings.claim: February–March has dense dates: 1–2 Mar 1354 Gelibolu earthquake, 3 Mar 1878 San Stefano, 6 Mar 1913 Yanya, 26 Mar 1913 Edirne falls, 29 Mar 1430 Selanik conquered.
findings.detail: Gelibolu: an earthquake on the night of 1–2 March 1354 destroyed the walls, and Süleyman Pasha took the town within about a month, the first Ottoman stronghold in Europe. San Stefano, signed 3 Mar 1878, is Bulgaria's Liberation Day, so tone matters. Yanya/Ioannina: surrendered 6 Mar 1913; some sources say 5 Mar, and 21 Feb is the Old Style date. Edirne/Adrianople captured by the Bulgarian army 26 Mar 1913 (BTA); one source gives 13 Mar, the Old Style date. Thessalonica: taken by storm by Murad II on 29 Mar 1430 after the 1422–30 siege.
findings.recommendation: Use 29 Mar (1430 conquest) and 8 Nov (1912 loss) as the page's 'Selanik bookends', a strong storytelling pair. On 3 Mar, tell the Rumeli Turkish experience of 1878 (the 93 Harbi refugees) without mocking Bulgaria's national day.
findings.verify_note: Wikipedia dates the Gallipoli earthquake to 2 March 1354, with Süleyman Pasha taking the town within about a month. BTA (26 Mar 2025) gives the capture of Adrianople as 26 March 1913 without saying whether that is Old or New Style; it is the New Style date, and 13 March is Old Style. Wikipedia confirms Thessalonica was taken by storm on 29 March 1430. I did not recheck San Stefano (3 Mar 1878) or Yanya (6 Mar 1913) in this pass; both match standard references.

findings.claim: April–May: İşkodra 22/23 Apr 1913; Kosovo Turks' National Day 23 Apr; exchange begins 1 May 1923; Hıdrellez 6 May; Atatürk's symbolic birthday 19 May; 1989 exodus from 20 May; Treaty of London 30 May 1913.
findings.detail: Scutari/İşkodra: Essad Pasha's surrender is dated 22 Apr (1913 Spectator) or 23 Apr (other sources), with the formal offer made 21 Apr. Kosovo Turks have celebrated 23 April as their national day annually since Kosovo's 2008 independence. Hıdrellez, 6 May, was inscribed by UNESCO in 2017 as a joint Turkey–North Macedonia element. 1989: on 20 May, Turks protested in Pristoe to demand their names back (BTA). Zhivkov announced the border opening 29 May. Turkey fully opened Kapıkule 3 Jun (some sources say 2 Jun). Turkey closed the border 22 Aug. About 310,000–322,000 people were expelled, about 360,000 including later family members. Treaty of London: 30 May 1913.
findings.recommendation: Run a 'Büyük Göç 1989' series 20 May–22 Aug 2027. It is the strongest migration-story UGC opportunity, since many followers' parents lived through it. Collect stories from April. Make 6 May a lighter Hıdrellez traditions-and-food week.
findings.verify_note: Wikipedia: Essad Pasha offered surrender on 21 Apr and it was accepted on 23 Apr 1913. UNESCO: Hıdrellez was inscribed in 2017 (12.COM) for Türkiye and North Macedonia, celebrated 6 May. BTA (20 May 2024): Pristoe demonstration on 20 May 1989. Wikipedia: Zhivkov announced the border opening on 29 May, Kapıkule fully opened 3 Jun (some say 2 Jun), and the border closed 21-22 Aug; 310,000-322,000 people were expelled, about 360,000 with later family members. Not verified: that Kosovo Turks have marked 23 April 'since Kosovo's 2008 independence'. Gazete Birlik (23 Apr 2026) confirms the holiday is celebrated but gives no origin.

findings.claim: June: Congress of Berlin opens 13 Jun 1878; Kosovo 1389 is 15 Jun (Julian) and is marked 28 Jun as Vidovdan; Soyadı Kanunu 21 Jun 1934.
findings.detail: The Congress of Berlin opened 13 Jun 1878 to revise San Stefano. Kosovo: 15 June 1389 in the Julian calendar; Serbia marks Vidovdan on 28 June in the modern calendar. Sultan Murad I and Prince Lazar both died, and the assassination story (Miloš Obilić) is partly legendary. Some blogs wrongly give '28 June 1389' as the historical date.
findings.recommendation: Post Kosovo on 15 June as 'Kosova 1389: Hüdavendigâr'ın şehadeti' with a myth-vs-fact angle. Mention 28 June only as the Serbian commemoration, and avoid triumphalist framing.
findings.verify_note: Wikipedia gives Kosovo as 15 June 1389 in the Julian calendar. The proleptic Gregorian equivalent is 23 June, and 28 June is only the modern Vidovdan date (Julian 15 June falling on Gregorian 28 June in the 20th-21st centuries). Murad I was killed. Wikipedia calls Miloš Obilić a legendary or 'mythological' figure, and the timing of the assassination is disputed. I did not recheck Berlin 13 Jun 1878, which is a standard date.

findings.claim: The page's founding dates are disputed: 1352 (Çimpe) and Edirne's conquest (1361 vs 1369). Address this openly as content rather than hiding it.
findings.detail: Çimpe/Tzympe: modern scholarship holds it was granted to Ottoman troops around 1352 as mercenaries in the Byzantine civil war. The traditional 1356 moonlight raid by Süleyman Pasha's 40 men is doubted, and a 2023 Turkish article argues the conquests began only after the 1354 earthquake. Edirne: TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi notes that 1361, 1362, 1367 and 1369 have all been proposed, with 1361 'gaining weight' in Turkish scholarship. Wikipedia reports that most modern scholars favour 1369 following Zachariadou's study of Byzantine sources.
findings.recommendation: Use this disclosure as a launch-week post: 'Neden 1352? Tarihçiler tartışıyor.' It builds credibility and draws expert comments. Never present 1361 as certain.
findings.verify_note: Wikipedia's Çimpe article: modern scholarship says Kantakouzenos handed the fortress over around 1352, while the traditional account is Süleyman Pasha's 1356 night raid. Minor detail: Wikipedia says 'thirty nine selected raiders', not 40 men. TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi: 1361, 1362, 1367 and 1369 have all been proposed, and '1361'de ele geçirildiği görüşü ağırlık kazanmaktadır.' The Wikiwand page for the 1369 / Zachariadou view returned 403, so I did not recheck it.

findings.claim: The Library of Congress Abdul Hamid II Collection (1,819 photos in 51 albums, about 1880–1893) has Rumeli images. Item records carry 'No known restrictions on publication'.
findings.detail: Checked via the LoC API on 2026-11-03. Searches returned 5 Monastir items, including '[Imperial military middle school, Monastir]' (2001700037) and '[High school, Monastir]' (2001700289); 2 Yanya high-school items (2001700290, Sébah & Joaillier, 1888–93); and 11 Edirne results. No hits for Salonica, Selanik, Üsküp or Prizren. The LoC disclaims owning rights and places assessment on the user, but these 1880s photos are public domain by age.
findings.recommendation: Build Manastır and Yanya then-vs-now posts from these images, credited 'Library of Congress, Abdul Hamid II Collection'. Do not imply Atatürk appears in them: the photos predate his time at the Manastır school.
findings.verify_note: Every loc.gov request, including item JSON for 2001700037, 2001700289 and 2001700290 and the collection pages, was blocked by a Cloudflare 403. I could not recheck the item IDs, the '1,819 photos in 51 albums' figure or the rights statement in this pass. These figures match the standard LoC description I knew before this check. The user should open the item pages directly.

findings.claim: SALT Research images are licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. 'No derivatives' means no cropping into templates, colourising or text overlays, which are exactly the edits Instagram now treats as making content original.
findings.detail: SALT's terms (archives.saltresearch.org): individual-research use under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, with attribution, no commercial use, and no alteration of the document. Other uses must be requested from salt.research@saltonline.org.
findings.recommendation: For SALT items, either post the image unaltered with commentary in the caption or a separate frame, or email SALT for permission. Prefer public-domain sources (LoC, Getty Open Content, Commons items with a verified PD tag) for edited or templated posts.
findings.verify_note: archives.saltresearch.org returned 403. I could not recheck the CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 terms or the contact email. The logic holds if the licence is ND: under the corrected P2, the edits that make a post count as original (added on-image context, graphics) would be derivatives.

findings.claim: Other safe image sources: Getty's Pierre de Gigord collection (6,000+ Ottoman photos, Open Content). Wikimedia Commons and Europeana are fine but need item-level checks. For İBB Atatürk Kitaplığı (92,312 postcards), reuse terms were not found.
findings.detail: Getty digitized the Gigord collection (96.R.14; 1853–1930 bulk) in 2018–19 under its Open Content Program. Commons' {{PD-Turkey}} covers authors dead more than 70 years or anonymous works published more than 70 years ago, and files must be PD in both Turkey and the US. Europeana accepts the Public Domain Mark and CC0, but a Kennisland study found recurring mislabelling. İBB Atatürk Kitaplığı: the collection size is on its site; licence terms were searched for and not found.
findings.recommendation: Keep a source sheet listing each image's URL, rights statement and credit line. For İBB postcards, ask the library before posting. Credit every image in the caption, which also signals originality and builds trust.
findings.verify_note: Smithsonian (8 Jan 2019) and Hyperallergic confirm the Pierre de Gigord collection: 6,000+ photos, accession 96.R.14, open under Getty's Open Content Program. The PD-Turkey template confirms Turkish terms: life plus 70, and 70 years from publication for anonymous works. The 'also PD in the US' rule is general Commons policy and is not on that template page. The İBB Atatürk Kitaplığı page returned 503, so neither the 92,312 count nor the terms were checked.

findings.claim: AI and colourisation: Meta applies an 'AI info' label (since July 2024) and requires users to disclose photorealistic AI video or realistic audio. Historians warn that colourised or AI-'restored' images shown without context mislead viewers.
findings.detail: Meta (Feb 2024) required disclosure for photorealistic video and realistic-sounding audio, with possible penalties. Still images were labelled automatically when detected. The 'Made with AI' label was renamed 'AI info' on 1 Jul 2024. PetaPixel (Oct 2020) reported historians urging creators to stop colourising and upscaling. Penang Monthly (Aug 2025) argues that AI-colourised images shared without context erode trust.
findings.recommendation: House rule: always show the original black-and-white image next to any colourised version and mark it 'Renklendirilmiştir / AI ile canlandırılmıştır'. Use Instagram's AI label for animated photos or AI voices. Never publish AI-generated scenes as historical photos. For a history page, credibility is the growth asset.
findings.verify_note: TechCrunch (1 Jul 2024) confirms 'Made with AI' was renamed 'AI info'. New since then: on 31 Aug 2026 Instagram renamed the 'AI creator' label to 'AI-generated profile'. It applies to profiles that feature an AI-generated person. Unlabeled profiles that Instagram detects may lose recommendation eligibility. This matters if the page ever uses an AI narrator persona. I did not recheck the Axios or PetaPixel 2020 items.

findings.claim: Platform risk: Turkey blocked Instagram nationwide for 9 days, 2–10 August 2024. A Turkey-based page relying on Instagram alone can lose its audience overnight.
findings.detail: Turkey's regulator blocked access on 2 Aug 2024 and lifted the block on 10 Aug after Meta agreed to cooperate (Euronews, Duvar English). NetBlocks called it the longest such ban on a major platform in recent years. Reports of social-media throttling in March 2025 could not be verified in this search.
findings.recommendation: From launch, cross-post Reels to YouTube Shorts and TikTok, and open a WhatsApp or Telegram channel linked from the bio, so the audience can be reached during an outage. Reuse the same voiceover and vertical edits.
findings.verify_note: Euronews (12 Aug 2024): Turkey blocked Instagram on 2 Aug 2024 and lifted the block on Saturday 10 Aug after assurances to the government. Duvar English returned 403, so the NetBlocks 'longest ban' quote is not verified. When cross-posting to TikTok or YouTube, note that Meta Sound Collection licences do not carry over (see F5), which is another reason to make voiceover the default audio.

missed_points: Under Instagram's own original-content guidelines (creators.instagram.com/original-content-guidelines, current), captions, credits, borders, watermarks and speed changes do not count as material edits. On-image text must do more than describe what is shown. The guidelines say nothing about archival or public-domain photos. For a page built on archive images, every post needs added information in the image itself (a map, a context overlay, a then-vs-now comparison) or a voiceover. The official test: 'if removing your contribution leaves the post essentially unchanged', add more of your own work. https://creators.instagram.com/original-content-guidelines

Instagram says you can check whether the account is still recommendable under Account Status, and appeal there. Eligibility returns when a 'significant percentage' of posts over a rolling 30 days is original. A weekly Account Status check is worth adding to the launch checklist. https://creators.instagram.com/blog/rewarding-original-creators-on-instagram (2026-04-30)

In the same 30 Apr 2026 post, Instagram names Collabs, Remix, and sharing to Stories or reposts as the right ways to use or credit others' content. Reposting a competitor's posts through those tools is the sanctioned route, not re-uploading. https://creators.instagram.com/blog/rewarding-original-creators-on-instagram

Edits now includes a carousel editor (iOS, 7 Oct 2026; Android 'coming soon') with shared canvases across slides, layout presets and saved brand presets. Useful for building consistent 'Kayıp Adlar' or 'Kurtuluş Takvimi' carousel templates. https://edits.instagram.com/blog/edits-carousel-editor

Meta Sound Collection tracks are licensed only for Facebook and Instagram, so a Reel with in-app music should not be cross-posted as-is to TikTok or YouTube Shorts (the E5 backup plan). Business accounts are limited to about 14,000 such tracks. https://www.foximusic.com/blog/instagram-reels-music-copyright-legal-guide/ (updated 2026-10-02)

Comment-to-DM rules: one private reply within 7 days of a comment, then only within 24 hours of each user reply. Automated DMs to people who have not engaged are, per Creatorflow, 'the single most common reason accounts get restricted.' The same logic warns against cold, scaled outreach to the competitor's 8,000 followers. I did not verify follow or unfollow rate limits. https://creatorflow.so/blog/automated-instagram-dms-creator-rules-safety/ (updated 2026-10-30)

The TBMM speech by Tekirdağ MP Enez Kaplan (10 Nov 2021) lists every Eastern Thrace district's November 1922 liberation date in one place. It is a handy master list for the 'Kurtuluş Takvimi' series, but it disagrees with TÜBA on Kırklareli (11 vs 10 Nov). https://tbmm.gov.tr/Milletvekili/UyeGenelKurulKonusmalariDetay?eid=100934

The Edirne glossary tags each entry with its exact source and village, e.g. 'fillemek: Kapıyı sürgülemek (DS.1866: Sarıcaali-Edirne)'. That makes it ready-made, citable material for 'Rumeli Sözlüğü' cards. https://www.paradigmaakademiyayinlari.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/edirne-yoresi-soz-varligi.pdf

Method limitation: the WebSearch budget for this turn was already used up when this review started. All checks were done by fetching cited and primary pages with WebFetch or curl. Pages that returned 403/404/503 or DNS errors (LoC, SALT, BetaNews, PetaPixel, Britannica, BNR, New East Archive, İBB, vienna.at, wikiwand) are marked unverifiable rather than confirmed.

Has Instagram's 'Your Algorithm' topic control (US launch 10 Dec 2025, announced to expand globally in English) reached Turkey or Turkish? Not confirmed.
Are the Trial Reels thresholds (1,000 followers, public account) still current in Nov 2026? Check the Instagram Help Center in the app.
Which Rumeli türküs exist in Instagram's in-app music library for a Creator account in Turkey? This needs checking on the phone.
